title: Compute Belief Reconstruction and Teacher-Action Losses
summary: A student can imitate a teacher action even when some environmental labels are unavailable.

frames: Action vectors use identical robot joint order; foot and support heights share a right-handed world frame with z up

units.values: Action targets and action scales use radians. Environmental features and their scales share declared normalized coordinates. Foot positions, terrain heights and clearance thresholds use meters; resulting normalized losses and violation rates are dimensionless.

physical_contract.axes: Batch B, synchronized time T, and declared action, environmental-feature or foot axes
physical_contract.timestamp_assumptions: Times are already aligned within each environment. A terrain label is constant across one supplied window. No resampling, recurrent state estimation or simulator stepping occurs.
physical_contract.batching: Batch B, synchronized time T, and declared action, environmental-feature or foot axes

provenance.authoring_notes: Original bounded teacher/student objective or terrain diagnostic associated with perceptive locomotion; no claim to reproduce the paper's recurrent gated network, training weights or hardware performance. All fixtures are synthetic.
